I know it’s more than most people would eat in one night, and I keep going until I feel really stuffed, almost sick. I hate that I do it, so I don’t invite anyone over. Honestly, I’ve started waiting until my kids are asleep so no one sees.

There are times when I feel this strange burst of energy—like I don’t need much sleep, and my mind races with ideas, booking trips for clients in record time or planning these big, elaborate vacations for myself that I know I can’t afford. I feel on top of the world for a few days, then crash—just foggy, low, and back to those late-night eating spells. But it never lasts more than a couple of days, so I don’t know if it’s really anything. Maybe I’m just burnt out. It’s been going on for a few months, on and off.
D023-D009_h001.question_a:

I’ll buy bags of snacks, frozen meals, just go through them all in one sitting. I know it’s way more than most people would eat in an evening, even on a treat night. I keep telling myself I’ll stop, but I don’t. I eat until my stomach hurts, until I’m groaning, but I still can’t put the food down.  

It’s worse when I’m alone. I plan it that way, actually—wait until my kids are with their dad, or after work when I’m home by myself. I’m so ashamed of how much I consume. I’d never want anyone to see me like that.  

Lately, I’ve had these bursts of energy—like I’m on fire. I’ll stay up until 3 a.m., rearranging travel itineraries for clients, feeling super focused, almost giddy. But it never lasts more than a day or two, and I don’t do anything reckless—no spending sprees, no wild decisions. It’s not mania, at least not the way I’ve read about it. I just get these short bursts, then crash into guilt about the binges. It’s the eating that’s ruining my life, not the mood swings.

I always do it alone, lights off, embarrassed to admit how much I’m consuming. The weird part is, a few days later, I’ll suddenly feel wired—like I can plan ten vacations in one night, need almost no sleep, talk a mile a minute on calls, even flirt with clients in ways I later regret. I feel amazing then, almost invincible, but it always crashes. These high periods don’t make me psychotic or hospitalized, but they’re definitely not me. This cycle—bingeing in shame, then surging with energy—has been going on long enough that I know it’s not just stress. I meet all the markers for both, but the mood swings confirm it’s more than just eating issues.
